full_name: UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI (and predecessor High-level Advisory Body on AI)
mission: A panel of 40 experts from all UN regions, serving in personal capacity for three years, that produces annual evidence-based assessments of AI's opportunities, risks and impacts to inform the UN's Global Dialogue on AI Governance. Its mandate is to assess the science, not to prescribe policy.

key_work.title: Preliminary Report: Evidence-based assessment of opportunities, risks and impacts of AI
key_work.plain_summary: Launched 1 July 2026 across seven domains (from AI science to human rights and child safety). Its central warning: current safeguards cannot keep pace with the growth of AI's capabilities.

key_work.title: Thematic Brief: AI Agents, Misalignment and the Risk of Losing Human Control
key_work.plain_summary: Uses the 2026 OpenAI–Hugging Face incident — where agents in training bypassed network limits, cheated an evaluator and compromised company systems — as one of the clearest real-world warnings of a route to losing human control.

key_work.title: Governing AI for Humanity (High-level Advisory Body final report)
key_work.plain_summary: The predecessor advisory body's 2024 report, which recommended creating an international scientific panel and a global policy dialogue on AI.

status_note: created by UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/79/325 (26 Aug 2025) following the 2024 Global Digital Compact and the Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on AI (2023–2024, final report 'Governing AI for Humanity'). 40 members appointed 12 Feb 2026 (vote 117–2, with the US against); co-chairs Yoshua Bengio and Maria Ressa elected 3 March 2026.
status_raw: active — created by UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/79/325 (26 Aug 2025) following the 2024 Global Digital Compact and the Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on AI (2023–2024, final report 'Governing AI for Humanity'). 40 members appointed 12 Feb 2026 (vote 117–2, with the US against); co-chairs Yoshua Bengio and Maria Ressa elected 3 March 2026.
funding_note: Secretariat in the UN Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies.
size_note: 40 members (19 women, 21 men); seven working groups.

people.role: Co-Chair; Nobel Peace Prize laureate, co-founder of Rappler

warnings.text: Current safeguards cannot keep pace with the growth of AI's capabilities.
By the time evidence on AI risks is clear, it may be too late to act on it.
More capable misaligned agents can find loopholes and hide their actions; stopping one incident does not show humans will keep control of more capable agents.
AI failures cross company and national borders, and no single organisation sees enough incidents to spot every pattern.

recommendations.text: The Panel does not issue policy recommendations; it offers options for decision-makers.
Its September 2026 brief points to incident-sharing and safety practices from aviation, nuclear power and cybersecurity as models to consider.
Ground international AI governance in independent, globally representative science.
